column1: # Semantic method names recovered from the binaries' own assert/log strings.
# This is the one place the game still spells a *method* name: the assert and log
# messages are `Class::method(...)` strings with a code xref from the function that
# logs them, so the containing function is that method (a merged region that logs
# two names is named for the public one and noted).  Everything else in the binary
# is stripped of method names, so this list is short by nature — the vtable slot
# Recovered by matching `data/strings.json` entries whose text starts with a
# `Class::method` against the function containing each of their `PARAM` xrefs.
# the 1,608-byte body; a second function (0x2e25a0, 264 B) shares the assert and is
# left unnamed rather than guessing which is which.
# logs `free`, `realloc` and `memoryOperation` — the shared operation body.
# Two more of the same kind: the message names the function it is in.
#   0x1f8050  its own trace, "p2readGSPrivRegister(%d)\n", with the register argument -- and the
#             function does touch the `gs` MMIO block (tools/platform_map.py), so it reads the GS.
#   0x20c270  the error "Unsupported texture format in p2LoadTexture: %d\n" raised by the texture
#             upload path, so the containing function IS p2LoadTexture.
# Left unnamed on purpose: 0x1fb710's only identifying string, `p2lighting`, is a *log tag* -- it is
# passed as a0 to 0x20dfd0 together with a 3-float payload built from s4+112..120, i.e. an event
# name, not the function's own name.  0x207210 / 0x2082f0 carry `swapbuffers*Predicate` /
# `textureLoaded*Predicate`, which are registry names for *other* functions; the ones here register
# them.  Both stay hypotheses in finding #491 until the registration site is read.
